gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Tektur bends its letters like bent wire, with every curve left open at the end. Noto Sans Bamum is the plain sans underneath, its big open counters doing the quiet, readable work the heading never tries to.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Distinctive outsized lowercase gives Tektur a strange, engineered personality, with no thick-and-thin contrast to slow the eye. And Noto Sans Bassa Vah settles in below with a swollen midsection and a pliers-like c, so a long passage feels dense and steady.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-batak: Approachable is the first word that comes to mind for Noto Sans Batak, with its towering x-height and an e that never squeezes shut. Tektur, bent from one length of tubing, sits over it like a signpost.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Noto Sans Bengali keeps its capitals barely taller than its lowercase, with distinctly open letter mouths. But a long stretch of it reads smoothly, a counterpoint to Tektur, which feels like following a single thread.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Noto Sans Brahmi sets its mean line high and leaves every curve open-ended. Tektur's curves never thin at the shoulders, so a long passage moves from wiry headline to this sans-serif text without a bump.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Noto Sans Buhid leaves generous space between curve ends and the stem, under a high-set x-height. But what really stands out is Tektur's single-thread line against that sans-serif body, one wiry and expressive, the other plainly readable.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-carian: Spaghetti-like lines, wiry and loose, define Tektur's look. Noto Sans Carian answers with terminals that stay apart like open scissor blades, so the sans text stays crisp beneath it.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Rounded-wire strokes make Tektur instantly recognizable, and it loves being expressive at display size. Noto Sans Chakma does the opposite job, packing its lowercase up toward the caps with open, uncrowded mouths for steady sans reading.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Wire-like and unmistakably quirky, Tektur sits above a tall band of letters with short stalks. Its strongest quality is that tension with Noto Sans Cherokee, whose e keeps a wide gap at the terminal.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-noto-sans-chorasmian: Noto Sans Chorasmian has a large x-height with short ascenders, and its curves stop short instead of closing in. But Tektur frames its counters with same-width strokes for display flair, while the sans-serif body simply keeps the text easy to follow.
